parental_leave_policy: Employees who have completed at least six months of continuous service are eligible for parental leave. Full-time employees receive sixteen weeks of paid parental leave following the birth, adoption, or foster placement of a child. Part-time employees receive a prorated number of weeks based on their average weekly hours over the preceding six months. Parental leave must be taken within twelve months of the qualifying event and can be split into two separate blocks with at least thirty days notice given to the employee's manager before each block begins. Employees on parental leave continue to accrue vacation time and remain enrolled in the company health plan at the same contribution rate as active employees.
remote_work_policy: Employees may work remotely up to three days per week with manager approval, and fully remote arrangements are available for roles designated as remote-eligible by their department head. Remote employees are expected to be available during core collaboration hours of ten in the morning to three in the afternoon in their local time zone. The company provides a one-time home office stipend of five hundred dollars for approved remote employees to purchase a monitor, chair, or desk. Equipment purchased with this stipend remains company property and must be returned upon termination of employment. Remote work arrangements are reviewed annually and can be revoked if performance or collaboration issues arise.
expense_reimbursement_policy: All business expenses must be submitted through the expense portal within thirty days of being incurred, along with an itemized receipt for any single expense over twenty-five dollars. Approved categories include travel, client meals up to a limit of one hundred dollars per person, professional development courses, and software subscriptions directly related to an employee's role. Expenses submitted after the thirty day window require written justification and manager approval before being processed. Reimbursements are typically paid out within two pay cycles of approval. Personal expenses, alcohol at non-client events, and first-class airfare are not eligible for reimbursement under any circumstances.
performance_review_policy: Formal performance reviews are conducted twice per year, in June and December, and are based on goals set collaboratively between the employee and their manager at the start of each review period. Reviews evaluate performance against role-specific competencies as well as progress toward individual goals, and result in a rating on a five-point scale ranging from does not meet expectations to significantly exceeds expectations. Compensation adjustments tied to performance are typically finalized within thirty days of the December review cycle. Employees who receive a rating of does not meet expectations are placed on a structured sixty day improvement plan with weekly check-ins with their manager.
paid_time_off_policy: Full-time employees accrue fifteen days of paid time off per calendar year during their first two years of employment, increasing to twenty days after two years and twenty-five days after five years of continuous service. Unused paid time off can be carried over into the following year up to a maximum of five days, with any remaining balance forfeited at the end of the carryover period. Employees must submit time off requests at least two weeks in advance for any absence longer than three consecutive days. Sick leave is tracked separately from paid time off and does not count against the annual accrual described here.
